title: Rewrite away type converting functions that do not convert types

timeline.message:
Rewrite away type converting functions that do not convert types

When a type converting function does not actually convert the type, it can be rewritten away. This opens the door for the resulting aliasing eval to also be rewritten into a project, which removes the ReferenceAttribute, and open the door for improved optimizations.

In particular it Fixes #107716
timeline.author: Craig Taverner

reply.body:
What, but this is _Java_ where unnecessary verbosity is the norm!

OK, seriously though, I like your suggestion. But since the 'suggested change' did not also include the call to this class, I changed it in a separate commit rather than just merging yours.

timeline.body:
super-duper nit: Could add an example, and could use `@link` in the javadoc to prevent this from getting stale if we rename/refactor our optimizer rules.
```suggestion
     * A following {@link ReplaceAliasingEvalWithProject} will effectively convert {@link ReferenceAttribute} into {@link FieldAttribute},
```

Hmm, why only in case of field attrs? Wouldn't this more general optimization also work?
```suggestion
                if (fa.dataType() == convert.dataType()) {
```

reply.body: I only changed FieldAttribute because my primary goal was to enable lucene optimizations done by physical planning, and ReferenceAttributes that hide FieldAttributes were the main issue. Expanding to a wider scope could make sense, but also does not change performance in any way at all. The current PR makes one query 75x faster! I was already mildly concerned that my changes would have some subtle unforeseen side-effects, so did not want to widen the scope beyond what I actually needed.

timeline.body: I think these two tests could be refactored into a single, parameterized test that goes over all relevant data types.

reply.body: Yes, but the `mapping-basic.json` mapping used for this entire class is lacking in type diversity to achieve that. Perhaps I should look around for other unit tests that do not do a complete index mapping for such coverage.
I realize I can just add a bunch of new fields to the mapping-basic.json, so I did that.
Well, that caused a lot of other tests to fail, due to the extra and unexpected fields, so I've made a new mapping file with these fields, used just in that test.
There is `mapping-all-types.json` that I used in the past for cases like this.

timeline.body:
LGTM.

If we want this to be extra nice, I think we could generalize it to not only work on `FieldAttributes`, but general expressions that are trivially converted to another type. If you decide to go for it, this would require only a couple additional tets, I think:
- Multiple (trivial) conversions in the same expression.
- Trivial conversions applied to reference attributes and to the output of functions.
Maybe one thing: This is a proper optimization, not a substitution. I'd expect this to be placed in the `operators` batch, among the `prune/elimination` optimization rules.

reply.body: But then it will happen after `ReplaceAliasingEvalWithProject` which will disable the optimization required. It is the replacement of the Eval with Project that converts the ReferenceAttribute into a FieldAttribute.
Essentially my rule needs to occur after `ReplaceStatsNestedExpressionWithEval` and before `ReplaceAliasingEvalWithProject` in order to have the desired effect.

+    support that we already have for MaxMind's 'GeoIP2 City' and 'GeoIP2
+    Country' databases -- that is, one would need to arrange their own
+    download management via some custom endpoint or otherwise arrange for
+    the relevant file(s) to be in the `$ES_CONFIG/ingest-geoip` directory on
+    the nodes of the cluster.

+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.Version
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.VersionProperties
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.util.GradleUtils
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.internal.info.BuildParams
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.testclusters.StandaloneRestIntegTestTask
+
+apply plugin: 'elasticsearch.internal-java-rest-test'
+apply plugin: 'elasticsearch.internal-test-artifact-base'
+apply plugin: 'elasticsearch.bwc-test'
+
+dependencies {
+  testImplementation project(path: ':x-pack:plugin:inference:qa:inference-service-tests')
+  compileOnly project(':x-pack:plugin:core')
+  javaRestTestImplementation(testArtifact(project(xpackModule('core'))))
+  javaRestTestImplementation project(path: xpackModule('inference'))
+  clusterPlugins project(
+    ':x-pack:plugin:inference:qa:test-service-plugin'
+  )
+}
+
+// inference is available in 8.11 or later
+def supportedVersion = bwcVersion -> {
+  return bwcVersion.onOrAfter(Version.fromString("8.11.0"));
+}
+
+BuildParams.bwcVersions.withWireCompatible(supportedVersion) { bwcVersion, baseName ->
+  def javaRestTest = tasks.register("v${bwcVersion}#javaRestTest", StandaloneRestIntegTestTask) {
+    usesBwcDistribution(bwcVersion)
+    systemProperty("tests.old_cluster_version", bwcVersion)
+    maxParallelForks = 1
+  }
+
+  tasks.register(bwcTaskName(bwcVersion)) {
+    dependsOn javaRestTest
+  }
+}

+        String responseStr = EntityUtils.toString(response.getEntity());

+  title: Add support for the 'Connection Type' database to the geoip processor
+  body: |-
+    Follow on to #107287, #107377, #108639, and #108651
+
+    Adds support for the ['GeoIP2 Connection
+    Type'](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/connection-type)
+    database from MaxMind to the `geoip` processor.
+
+    The `geoip` processor will automatically download the [various
+    'GeoLite2'
+    databases](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/geolite2-free-geolocation-data),
+    but the 'GeoIP2 Connection Type' database is not a 'GeoLite2' database
+    -- it's a commercial database available to those with a suitable license
+    from MaxMind.
+
+    The support that is being added for it in this PR is in line with the
+    support that we already have for MaxMind's 'GeoIP2 City' and 'GeoIP2
+    Country' databases -- that is, one would need to arrange their own
+    download management via some custom endpoint or otherwise arrange for
+    the relevant file(s) to be in the `$ES_CONFIG/ingest-geoip` directory on
+    the nodes of the cluster.
+  notable: true
